outcome: No new edge proposed. Every lead to an existing endpoint was either already represented, rests on topic alone, or could not be read lawfully. Her three current edges (critique of anthropology; settler colonialism via Kauanui; Indigenous-authored history) stand.

edges_considered_not_proposed.reason: Searched without a verified omission. The 1991 essay was re-read 2026-10-31 in the University of Hawaiʻi repository PDF (pp. 159–167, with references) and searched for every atlas person endpoint: it names Keesing, Linnekin and Kameʻeleihiwa (none are endpoints) and no atlas person. Hobsbawm and Ranger's invention-of-tradition volume is not cited by name in her essay (Linnekin's reply, p. 172, says Keesing misreads that literature), so no hobsbawm edge.

Already represented: Kauanui's note 7 (2016) listing Trask's 'settlers of color' essay among analyses before Wolfe is the basis of edge_2144 to Settler colonialism. A person↔person edge would restate Kauanui's precedence claim as a relationship between Trask and Wolfe that neither is shown to have made.

Held, unread. Smith's Decolonizing Methodologies (1999) may cite From a Native Daughter, but the atlas extract read covers only pp. 1–5, and the Trent University lending scan refused full-text search (access-restricted). Do not add without reading Smith's citation.
Searched without a verified omission: Simpson's 'On Ethnographic Refusal' (Junctures 9, 2007; journal PDF, 14 pp.) was searched 2026-10-31 for Trask, Keesing and Hawaiʻi; none occur.

Not proposed. A 2001 student-newspaper report says she quoted Fanon in a lecture; From a Native Daughter (1993/1999) is unread (no lawful full text found), so its debts to Fanon or Said are unknown. A student report of a lecture is not enough for an edge.
Topic only (Pacific Indigenous critiques of academic history); no named exchange found.
